slices.title: Map existing ID stores to explicit port boundaries
slices.goal: Establish a source-accurate seam map that keeps blob, event, world, and sync stores distinct and gives port design an explicit ownership baseline.
slices.enables: Document and type the existing blob, event, world, and sync store seams without merging their authority; identify consumer-owned files and compatibility adapters.

oracle.expected: The architecture boundary names blob/event/world/sync stores separately and a fixture rejects their flattening.
oracle.verifier: The seam-map classification table and compile-time trait ownership test.

slices.rollback: Revert the documentation/test additions; no runtime behavior or persisted bytes change.

slices.title: Define versioned capability-oriented port contracts
slices.goal: Phase 1 root owner: land the common interface and private module-root skeletons before consumer adapters add leaf modules. Do not declare or export absent leaf modules. After this PR merges, this slice relinquishes shared-root writes; consumers do not edit roots.
slices.enables: Introduce separate store, blob, event-log, world, object-bucket, stream, and request-transport contract types with capability declarations, semantic guarantees, limits, and typed unsupported errors. Include a Kafka-like ordered-stream test double to verify additive supportability without selecting or implementing Kafka. This is the sole owner of common crate root exports/Cargo manifests and the shared test-vector schema; consumers add distinct module files and do not edit those roots. Owns stable crate-root exports/Cargo manifests and shared test-vector schema. The `federation/mod.rs`, `graph/mod.rs`, and `triples/mod.rs` files define roots only; they do NOT unconditionally export absent future feature modules. V2/V3 feature exports are wired by 9110-09 after exact module outputs exist, with a release gate. Consumers own distinct child modules and do not edit roots. The Kafka-like ordered-stream double is in-memory contract coverage only, not a Kafka adapter or deployment choice. The B registry inventory is exactly b01_key_lifecycle, b02_key_revocation, b03_replay_guard, b04_signature_suites, b05_signer_binding, b06_rejection_events, b07_conflict_report, b08_sync_scope, b09_anti_entropy, b15_peer_priority, b16_fanout_budget, b17_query_grants, b18_query_privacy, b19_signed_receipt, b20_request_identity, b21_result_dedup, b22_loop_inform, b23_routing_state, b24_topology_probe, b25_local_reputation, b27_claim_log, b28_takeover_response, b29_receipt_contradiction, b30_search_integrity, b31_peer_classes, and b32_ingest_gate under federation/slices/. The registry file records these exact paths but leaves not-yet-built modules unexported.

oracle.expected: Capability negotiation chooses the ordered-stream profile only when declared; in-memory duplicate/retry traces conform without a Kafka client or runtime dependency.
oracle.verifier: A small independent ordered-stream reference state machine checks sequence, redelivery, ack, and unsupported-capability outcomes.

slices.rollback: Keep existing adapters and data formats; remove or revise only unused additive exports after all consumers are migrated. Never remove a module/root still imported by a consumer.

slices.title: Specify redb and Turso/SQLite capability profiles
slices.goal: Provide honest redb and Turso/libSQL capability profiles, including bounded atomic scope and explicit timeout/unknown-commit behavior.
slices.enables: Implement required port profiles for redb and Turso/libSQL; state transaction, durability, scan, retry, and timeout ambiguity semantics without claiming identical atomicity.

requires.description: consume owned contract only; do not wait for full sibling program

oracle.expected: redb and Turso profiles report only declared transaction scopes; an injected lost response remains unknown until stable-ID readback.
oracle.verifier: An abstract store state machine plus a fault injector independent of either adapter.

slices.rollback: Keep the prior adapter selection/config active; do not migrate or rewrite persisted data on rollback.

slices.title: Build shared store conformance fixtures and capability reports
slices.goal: Make adapter behavior decidable through a shared state-machine corpus and machine-readable capability reports.
slices.enables: Create portable conformance vectors and machine-readable required/optional capability reports; run the suite against redb and Turso/SQLite, with IndexedDB profile reserved for its verdict.

oracle.expected: Adapter observations match reference CRUD, scan, transaction, retry, and capability-negotiation transitions.
oracle.verifier: A deterministic abstract state machine that emits expected state and capability report.

slices.rollback: Disable the new conformance runner without changing adapter runtime selection or stored data.

slices.title: Prototype IndexedDB adapter for bounded conformance evaluation
slices.goal: Implement an isolated IndexedDB request-batch prototype that exercises the declared browser-store capability subset without deciding product adoption.
slices.enables: Produce browser conformance results for transaction lifetime, quota/eviction, upgrades, and reopen behavior. #9082 owns the adopt/defer/reject decision; this prototype remains disabled by default.

requires.description: consume owned contract only; do not wait for full sibling program

oracle.expected: IndexedDB either passes the required browser subset or produces an explicit unsupported-capability verdict; it never advertises a long-lived async transaction.
oracle.verifier: Shared store fixtures executed in supported browsers and a per-engine capability matrix.

slices.rollback: Default to evaluate-only; do not enable IndexedDB in production. If evaluation fails, retain existing browser persistence and remove the experimental adapter.
slices.design_section: V2 — stable seams and conformance foundation (first implementation target)

slices.title: Implement ordered lifecycle hooks and fixed acceptance gate
slices.goal: Route every retained-data ingress through the fixed signed/validated gate and deterministic extension lifecycle, including commit-time policy reauthorization.
slices.enables: Add typed prepare/commit/outbox lifecycle hooks with deterministic order, bounded context, reentrancy policy, typed errors, and an unbypassable signature/validation/replay/tenant authorization gate; local producers sign before admission. Enumerate all normal paths before claiming completeness; see 9110-13.

oracle.expected: No hook/local path accepts an unsigned, invalid, replayed, or unauthorized retained object; revoked policy blocks commit and retry.
oracle.verifier: Generated admission trace model with independently evaluated gate invariants.

slices.rollback: Revert the extension implementation only while retaining the fixed signed/validated gate; security invariants are not rollback switches.

slices.title: Add durable outbox recovery and at-least-once hook delivery
slices.goal: Recover post-commit event delivery safely across restart with stable IDs and at-least-once semantics.
slices.enables: Persist post-commit events within advertised transaction scope, replay by stable ID after restart, and expose quarantine/reconciliation when store and stream cannot commit atomically.

oracle.expected: Every committed operation is either delivered at least once or remains visibly pending/quarantined across restart; no unknown outcome is labeled rollback.
oracle.verifier: Crash-injected outbox state machine keyed by durable operation/event IDs.

slices.rollback: Disable outbox delivery only after preserving committed operation records for operator replay; never delete or replay with new IDs.

slices.title: Prototype additive NATS stream adapter
slices.goal: Prove a second ordered-stream adapter can fit the stable port without changing core semantics; do not build a Kafka product adapter.
slices.enables: Demonstrate a second stream/transport adapter using existing stable contracts and document ack, ordering, redelivery, replay, retention, and limits; do not promise exactly-once.

requires.description: Requires the stable stream port contract.

oracle.expected: A contract-only ordered stream test passes duplicate/restart traces without a Kafka client or runtime adapter.
oracle.verifier: In-memory ordered-stream reference model; no Kafka implementation is built.

slices.rollback: Do not enable the adapter unless selected; remove the optional test adapter without altering core stream contract.

slices.title: Add Postgres capability profile without core changes
slices.goal: When selected by an owning deployment, add a Postgres profile as an additive adapter without changing core ports.
slices.enables: Implement an optional Postgres adapter against stable ports and publish its capability/conformance report; only proceed when an owning deployment chooses it.

requires.description: Requires stable port contracts before an adapter can be implemented.

oracle.expected: Only a deployment that selects Postgres enables the adapter, and its declared profile passes the common port suite without core API changes.
oracle.verifier: An independent port compatibility harness and capability report; no Postgres client is required before the explicit trigger.

slices.rollback: Contingent: if selected deployment fails conformance, withdraw Postgres from config and keep the prior backend; no data migration occurs automatically.
slices.trigger: Only when an owning deployment selects Postgres; until then keep the adapter as a V4 parked horizon item.

slices.title: Define versioned configuration schema and hard invariants
slices.goal: Establish the minimum validated V2 config contract needed before admission gates consume configuration.
slices.enables: Specify canonical versioned ConfigDocument, hard non-overridable ceilings, config validation errors, mechanism-versus-behavior classification, and secure unknown-field policy. This minimal schema is a V2 prerequisite for core gates.

requires.description: consume owned contract only; do not wait for full sibling program

oracle.expected: Canonical V2 config rejects any attempt to disable fixed gates and resolves deterministically.
oracle.verifier: Independent schema/reference validator with generated invalid-config matrix.

slices.rollback: Reject the candidate config schema and keep the last valid version; fixed admission invariants remain compiled and enforced.

slices.title: Implement mode bundles and safe override precedence
slices.goal: Resolve mode and scoped behavioral defaults deterministically while enforcing invariant, authority, and resource ceilings.
slices.enables: Resolve deployment mode defaults with documented precedence through tenant, peer/link/storage scopes and permitted operation overrides; ensure scopes remain distinct and non-special.

requires.description: consume owned contract only; do not wait for full sibling program

oracle.expected: Layered behavior overrides resolve in order within authority/resource ceilings, including both loosening and tightening examples.
oracle.verifier: Independent pure reference resolver and checked-in precedence examples.

slices.rollback: Restore the previous resolved config revision; already-completed external effects remain explicit and are not claimed undone.

slices.title: Model peer, link, storage, tier, and namespace planes independently
slices.goal: Keep peer, link, storage, tier, and namespace settings as distinct typed planes with explicit composition rules.
slices.enables: Define typed references and validation rules so peer class, link kind, storage capability/durability, data tier, and namespace registry can compose without implying one another.

requires.description: consume owned contract only; do not wait for full sibling program
consume owned contract only; do not wait for full sibling program

oracle.expected: Invalid combinations cannot infer peer trust from link kind or authorization from storage/tier selection.
oracle.verifier: A typed plane model and exhaustive invalid-combination matrix.

slices.rollback: Restore prior bindings; preserve independent peer/link/storage authorization checks.

slices.title: Add capability negotiation and downgrade rejection
slices.goal: Negotiate only mutually supported protocol/capability versions and reject security-weakening downgrades.
slices.enables: Negotiate highest mutually allowed version and required capabilities, bind negotiation to authenticated identities, and reject downgrade that removes mandatory security/correctness semantics.

requires.description: consume owned contract only; do not wait for full sibling program

oracle.expected: Negotiation selects the highest allowed common capability set and rejects security-weakening downgrade offers.
oracle.verifier: Adversarial protocol-negotiation state machine and signed transcript vectors.

slices.rollback: Reject negotiation/config change and continue only with a previously allowed protocol version; never downgrade past a security floor.

slices.title: Stage config activation and rollback by revision
slices.goal: Activate configuration revisions only after capability validation and provide rollback to prior configuration without rollback fiction for external effects.
slices.enables: Validate new config against all selected adapter capabilities before activation, expose resolved digest/provenance, retain prior revision for rollback, and document non-rollbackable external effects.

oracle.expected: A bad adapter/config never activates; rollback selects the exact previous revision and does not claim to undo external effects.
oracle.verifier: Config rollout state machine with injected validation failures and irreversible-effect markers.

slices.rollback: Restore the prior config revision; external side effects require explicit compensating operations.

slices.enables: Test exact existing serde JSON bytes against compatibility vectors; define deterministic-CBOR profile as a separate new format; do not silently re-sign or change legacy bytes.

requires.description: Use the completed legacy-preimage research report and vectors before implementing the compatibility test.
consume its typed identity-profile contract; not a blocker on its unrelated implementation

oracle.expected: Legacy signature bytes verify unchanged, while any new signed-envelope profile excludes its signature and IDs from the canonical Body preimage.
oracle.verifier: Independent Ed25519 verification against checked-in compatibility vectors and a second canonical-CBOR encoder.

slices.rollback: Keep legacy serde JSON verification and bytes unchanged; disable only new-profile writes/read support if compatibility vectors fail.

slices.title: Inventory every normal path through admission and hooks
slices.goal: Produce a complete path-to-gate inventory and test oracle before claiming hook/admission extensibility coverage.
slices.enables: Track every ingress/read/write/sync/query/stream/bucket path, gate/hooks, bypass test and recovery semantics; leave explicit unmigrated entries and block completeness claim until covered.

oracle.expected: Every normal retained-data path in the inventory maps to a fixed gate and a bypass test; any unmapped path blocks completion.
oracle.verifier: A path-to-test coverage matrix independently reviewed against source/call-site inventory.

slices.rollback: Mark incomplete paths unsupported/blocked; never roll back by opening a bypass around the fixed gate.
